Q: Grey out emoji characters (HTML / CSS) A:

Although applying grayscale is a valid approach, I would like to share a MUCH more simple approach. In unicode there is a thing called "Variation Selector 15" that basically makes emojis look monochrome - render them as text. All you need is to enter emoji followed by unicode sequence \uFE0E. Here is a wiki article

Here are a couple of examples:

✏️ - ✏︎
📂 - 📂︎ 
⚙️ - ⚙︎
🎨 - 🎨︎
👎 - 👎︎

In my opinion, they usually tend to look better than with filter: greyscale(100%). But be sure to test thoroughly - some emojis on some systems are always rendered as images. E.g. I see monochrome emojis on PC, but on android phone half of them is still colorful.

Q: Bind a socket to several IP addresses A:

Does your machine have three different IP addresses? Or do you have three servers with each an static IP? Binding to 0.0.0.0 should work, but may try to run as root.

Q: Eventhandling of Forms-timer and System-timer in PowerShell A:

  • The PowerShell engine can only process events registered for via Register-ObjectEvent while it is in control of the foreground thread.

  • A .ShowDialog() call puts Windows Forms in charge of the foreground thread, blocking PowerShell's event processing until after the form (dialog) is closed.

Solution options:

  • Use a System.Windows.Forms.Timer instance instead, and subscribe to its Tick event via an add_Tick() call, and perform the desired processing inside the script block passed to the call.

  • Forgo a .ShowDialog() call in favor of a non-blocking .Show() call, which requires subsequently entering a loop with periodic [System.Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents() calls.

See this answer for details.

Q: 1-D subpixel barcode recognition A:

This is a clean Code 39 containing 12345. This shows you what should have been visible in your picture, but isn't.

As you can see, the picture you have simply does not have the optical resolution to resolve the barcode. It is too blurry. Take for example the five narrow bars in the middle. In your picture, they are one gray rectangle with not even a hint of there being five separate bars.

The picture you have cannot be decoded by trivial means. Any method that might decode your picture would count as a super-resolution method. It would have to make assumptions about the picture that would be a gamble to make.

Such witchcraft might be present in commercially available specialist barcode reading software. Expect that to be expensive.

Everyone else would just solve the problem by taking clearer pictures.
